messages:
alex: Postmortem follow-up from yesterday's LB/DNS incident — quick sync on open action items and owners. TL;DR: recurring cross-region retry spike caused by stale SNI->route cache plus an LB config edge-case. Need owners, short timelines, and a rollout plan.

alex: Current open items (high level):
- immediate mitigation: force cache refresh and tighten SNI TTLs (short-term).
- config fix: make LB reject invalid SNI->origin mappings instead of silently falling back.
- testing: synthetic cross-region traffic + chaos probe to validate fallback behavior.
- monitoring: add a retry-storm alert with region breakdown and SNI mismatch tags.

alex: Assigning volunteers — please ack and give ETA.

maria: @alex I can own the immediate mitigation + tests. ETA for patch: end of day tomorrow. Plan: add explicit refresh endpoint and reduce TTL from 30s -> 10s for impacted routes, plus a unit test for stale-kv behavior.

sam: I'll pick up the LB config change to reject invalid mappings. Need to coordinate with infra deploy window. ETA: I can have a PR by Thu EOD, aiming for next canary.

leo: I'll build the chaos probe for cross-region retries and add a runbook. Will integrate into perf-ci. ETA: Fri noon.

natalie: I'll own monitoring and dashboards. Proposed new alert: retry_rate > 2% for 5m with region/SNI tags -> P1. Will add a Grafana panel and a pager rule. ETA: tomorrow morning.

ops-bot: Incident linked: REM-2026-042. Postmortem doc: https://redwood.internal/pm/REM-2026-042. /remind @maria in 1 day to follow up.

alex: Nice. Two extra notes: 1) We saw one TLS handshake pattern where client SNI arrived as "legacy-prod" and LB silently routed to fallback origin causing increased TLS renegotiation. Need regression test. 2) Cross-region egress path had intermittent connection resets that amplified retries.

maria: For the TLS handshake regression test I'll add a small harness that simulates legacy SNI header combos and assert the LB rejects/handles them as configured. Posting a snippet for review:

```
# local test to simulate SNI mismatch
openssl s_client -connect lb-test.redwood:443 -servername legacy-prod.example.com 
```

sam: FYI on deploy constraints: rejecting mappings is a schema change for LB config; we'll need a blue-green rollout to avoid dropping traffic unexpectedly. Suggest canary to 5% for 1 hour with automatic rollback on errors.

alex: Agreed — canary + auto-rollbacks. Add gating: synthetic probe must pass 10m of steady-state with <0.5% retry rate before widening.

leo: For chaos probe I'll wire a nightly job and a quick manual run command. Will add a healthcheck that fails the canary if retry spikes.

natalie: Adding alert runbook entry: first responder checks SNI mismatch logs -> if >20 mismatches in 5m escalate to network oncall. I'll add sample queries.

maria: Quick status update: started work on refresh endpoint, pushed initial branch: `git@repo:redwood/infra#sni-refresh-patch`. Need review from @sam for LB schema compatibility.

sam: Reviewing now. Left a couple inline comments about schema versioning and migration path.

alex: Good progress. Two outstanding decisions we need to call before Thursday:
- default SNI TTL and whether to make 10s global (maria proposal) or targeted per-route.
- whether LB should reject unknown SNI by default or opt-in.

natalie: My vote: targeted TTL on high-traffic routes first, rollout global after 2 weeks of stable metrics. For reject behavior, opt-in with a policy flag per customer until we complete compatibility tests.

sam: Agree with opt-in for safety. We'll add an admin flag and a migration doc.

alex: OK — decision: start targeted TTL change + opt-in reject flag. Action owners recap: 
- maria: SNI refresh + tests (ETA: tomorrow EOD)
- sam: LB schema + PR for reject behavior + migration doc (ETA: Thu EOD)
- leo: chaos probe + canary gating (ETA: Fri noon)
- natalie: monitoring + alert + runbook (ETA: tomorrow morning)

alex: Please update the postmortem doc with your PR links and set the incident action item to "In Progress" when you start. I'll follow up in 24h for a status rollup.

maria: Acked. I'll mark REM-2026-042 -> In Progress once patch branch opens a PR.

sam: Ack.

leo: Ack.

natalie: Ack.

alex: One last thing — we observed this pattern 3 times in last 90 days across different routes. We should add a recurring review: monthly networking resilience retro to surface these patterns and drive cross-team mitigations. Who wants to co-chair?

leo: I can co-chair with @alex.

alex: Thanks — adding to calendar: monthly resilience retro, first run next Monday.

ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: @alex @maria @sam @leo @natalie weekly follow-up every Tue 09:00 until REM-2026-042 is closed.

alex: Great — thanks everyone. I'll post a short summary in the postmortem doc and close the loop once we have canary results. :thumbsup:
